title: a reseal on a host that cannot run a tooth does not replace a seal from a host that can
intention: A run whose every failing tooth reads UNRAN (a host-bound tooth this host cannot run) writes no red seal: the standing record stays byte-identical and the result says the tooth was not run and by which host it can be. A run where a tooth actually FAILs still writes red.
why: Measured: 2026-11-20 on akiendell (Windows): cc_0's Linux landing of 80a2-fix (a2f477928) resealed bin/proofs/test_cairn_runs_from_cmd_with_no_bash.py on Linux, where teeth 1 and 3 read UNRAN (cairn.cmd is Windows-only), and persist_validation REPLACED my green 3 of 3 Windows seal with that red. The replacement voided 380d524e6e9c's hollow evidence and left the proof red on main until I resealed on Windows (bdce17bf1) and re-ran the hollow (1e958634f). Outline 9.4.8.1 already reads a not-run tooth as not-run, never red; the seal write has no such reading.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured); Law 5 (the repo is the state of the machine: a crossing's record is committed where it lands); Law 9 (green is earned).
how: Amended 2026-11-20 after reading the git history of the 380d seal: a shared guard in the tester (one helper both write paths call) refuses to persist a record whose teeth_red are all UNRAN, returning a not-run outcome that names the teeth. The proof runs on Linux with a fixture proof and an injected tester, so no host-bound tooth is needed to measure it.

clauses.claim: a fixture proof with a green seal, run on a host where every failing tooth reads UNRAN, through reseal() and through the cairn test --seal write, leaves the validations file byte-identical and the result names the UNRAN teeth as not run
the same run where one failing tooth is not UNRAN still writes red
a run that goes green still writes green

decisions.text: D1: reseal() writes no red when every failing tooth reads UNRAN.
D2: the cairn test --seal write in device.py applies the same rule.
D3: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause.

measured.saw: the first wording of this ticket (keep a green seal for the same fingerprint) would NOT have prevented tonight's swap: the Windows seal on bin/validations/test_cairn_runs_from_cmd_with_no_bash.json carried source_fingerprint 452ab81c239e, 80a2-fix (a2f477928) edited bin/cairn.py, inside that proof's closure, so the Linux reseal's record carried d1068249ba20 (red, 2 teeth red) over a seal that was already stale. reseal() also returns 'unchanged' before any run when a seal stands, so a same-fingerprint fixture never reaches the write. The defect is the red written for a not-run tooth (outline 9.4.8.1: not-run, never red); and two paths write seals, reseal.py and device.py (cairn test --seal).
